neighbours.label: a physical process reaching a state under pressure or heat (pressurised/pressurized, boil, increase speed)
fire: Trapped beneath the rock, the steam becomes pressurised and eventually bursts out.
The cabin is pressurized so that passengers can breathe at high altitude.
Engineers heated the tank enough to boil the remaining coolant away.
As the piston moves down, the air inside the cylinder is pressurized.
The pilot opened the throttle to increase speed before the climb.
Water in the sealed boiler is pressurised until the valve releases it.
The reactor core grew hot enough to boil the surrounding water.
Gas pumped into the chamber is pressurized to ten atmospheres.
quiet: Trapped beneath the rock, the fossil stayed hidden for millions of years.
The cabin is decorated so that passengers feel relaxed during the flight.
Engineers painted the tank before shipping it to the new plant.
As the sun moves down, the air over the valley grows quiet.
The pilot greeted the passengers before the flight to Denver.
Water in the garden pond is cleaned every spring by volunteers.
The reactor building was visited by students from the local school.
Gas prices in the region rose sharply during the winter months.

notes: Top: 'pressur-ised', 'ventr-icle', 'increase speed', 'boil', 'pressur-ized'. Testing the pressure/heat physical-process sense.
